overview.description: Comprehensive tile installation services covering bathrooms, showers, floors, backsplashes, outdoor areas, and specialty applications. Includes demolition, substrate preparation, waterproofing, tile setting, grouting, and sealing across residential and commercial projects.
overview.installationTime: 1-10 days depending on scope and complexity

materials.name: Ceramic Tile
materials.durability: Good — suitable for walls and light-traffic floors; wide variety of colors and sizes

materials.name: Porcelain Tile
materials.durability: Excellent — low water absorption (<0.5%), frost-resistant, scratch-resistant

materials.name: Large Format Porcelain (24x48+)
materials.durability: Excellent — fewer grout lines, seamless modern appearance

materials.name: Natural Stone (Marble, Travertine, Slate)
materials.durability: Good with proper sealing — marble is softer and etches; slate and granite are harder-wearing

materials.name: Glass Mosaic
materials.durability: Excellent water resistance; fragile on impact; best for vertical surfaces and accents

materials.name: Subway Tile (3x6 / 4x8 Ceramic or Porcelain)
materials.durability: Good — timeless profile, widely available, easy to replace individual tiles

materials.name: Cement / Encaustic Tile
materials.durability: Good — porous, requires sealing; develops patina over time
materials.maintenanceLevel: High — seal before grouting and annually thereafter

materials.name: Penny Tile / Hex Mosaic
materials.durability: Excellent — mesh-mounted sheets for consistent spacing
materials.maintenanceLevel: Medium — more grout lines to clean and maintain

techniques.name: Modified Thin-Set Mortar
techniques.description: Polymer-modified cement mortar providing superior bond strength and flexibility. The industry standard for most tile installations on cement board, plywood, and concrete substrates.

techniques.name: Mastic (Type 1 Adhesive)
techniques.description: Pre-mixed organic adhesive with fast grab. Suitable only for dry interior walls — not rated for wet areas or floors subject to movement.

techniques.name: Mud-Set (Mortar Bed)
techniques.description: Traditional sand-cement mortar bed floated to precise slope and flatness. Required for shower pans and curbless entries, and preferred when substrate is significantly out of level.

techniques.name: Dry-Lay / Test Layout
techniques.description: Full tile layout without adhesive to plan cuts, verify pattern alignment, and minimize waste before committing. Essential for complex patterns and expensive materials.

techniques.name: Back-Buttering
techniques.description: Applying thin-set to both the substrate and the back of each tile to achieve 95%+ coverage. Required for large format tiles, natural stone, and all wet-area installations.

techniques.name: KERDI / Liquid Membrane Waterproofing
techniques.description: Sheet membrane (Schluter KERDI) or liquid-applied membrane (RedGard, Hydroban) creates a continuous waterproof envelope behind tile in wet areas.

techniques.name: Uncoupling Membrane (DITRA / STRATA_MAT)
techniques.description: Polyethylene membrane installed between substrate and tile to prevent crack transmission, provide waterproofing, and allow vapor management.

techniques.name: Tile Leveling System
techniques.description: Clips and wedges used during installation to ensure lippage-free results. Critical for large format tiles and rectified edges where any unevenness is highly visible.

patterns.name: Subway / Running Bond
patterns.description: Classic offset brick pattern with each row shifted 50%. Timeless and versatile — works in every room from bathrooms to kitchens.

patterns.name: Herringbone
patterns.description: Rectangular tiles arranged in a V-shaped zigzag at 45 degrees. Adds movement and visual interest; makes narrow spaces feel wider.

patterns.name: Stacked / Straight Lay
patterns.description: Tiles aligned in a perfect grid with no offset. Clean, contemporary look that requires exceptionally flat substrate and precise tile sizing.

patterns.name: Diagonal (45-Degree)
patterns.description: Square tiles rotated 45 degrees to the wall. Makes small rooms feel larger and disguises walls that are not perfectly square.

patterns.name: Basketweave
patterns.description: Pairs of rectangular tiles alternating horizontal and vertical to create a woven appearance. Classic pattern common in traditional and transitional homes.

patterns.name: Chevron
patterns.description: Tiles cut at an angle to form a continuous V-shape pointing in one direction. More dynamic than herringbone with a modern edge.

patterns.name: 1/3 Offset (Brick Lay)
patterns.description: Similar to running bond but with a 33% offset instead of 50%. Reduces lippage risk with large format tiles while maintaining a classic look.

climateConsiderations: Freeze-thaw cycles (Nov-Mar) can crack improperly waterproofed or exterior installations — use frost-resistant porcelain rated for outdoor use
Heated tile floors (radiant heat) are popular due to harsh winters — DITRA-HEAT and Nuheat systems common in renovations
High humidity fluctuations between summer and winter require flexible thin-set and proper expansion joints
Salt and sand tracked in during winter months make durable, low-maintenance floor tile essential for entryways
Older Boston-area homes (pre-1950) often have uneven subfloors requiring leveling compounds or mud-set installations
popularStyles: Classic subway tile in brownstone and triple-decker renovations
Large format porcelain in modern condo builds (Seaport, Assembly Row)
Handmade zellige and artisan tile in Cambridge/Somerville remodels
Marble accents in luxury Back Bay and Beacon Hill bathrooms
Wood-look porcelain plank tile for open-plan living areas
Encaustic cement tile in Victorian-era home restorations
